name: PhiX174 (ΦX174 bacteriophage)
short_description: The smallest known DNA phage, and tailless: a simple icosahedral shell built from four different capsid proteins, with short spikes at its twelve vertices instead of a docking apparatus. Its genome is a single-stranded, circular loop of DNA only about 5,400 bases long.

textbook.1: FAIL on gemini-3-pro-image, attempt 1. Correct tailless compact icosahedral shell, correct single-strand DNA (one continuous golden thread coiling on itself, no double-helix look), correct internal pilot-protein blob and DNA-binding dots. BUT SPIKE COUNT MEASURED WRONG: a systematic crop-by-crop count (14 candidate blobs, one confirmed false-positive on the cutaway window's rim glass-shading, one pair merged into a single bottom knob) found 13 genuine, individually-verified spike knobs on the visible hemisphere alone -- geometrically impossible for a 12-vertex icosahedron and traced to the model adding extra knobs along the freshly-cut edge of the cutaway window, not just at the true vertices. Rejected; re-rendered with an explicit 'exactly twelve vertices total, none on the cut rim' instruction.
textbook.2: PASS on gemini-3-pro-image, attempt 2 (prompt explicitly capped the count at twelve true vertices and forbade knobs on the cutaway's cut edge). SPIKE COUNT MEASURED: a full-image recount, going clockwise around the whole visible silhouette and cross-checking against the previous attempt's inflated count, found exactly 12 distinct, individually-separated spike knobs, all sitting on the shell's true corner vertices and NONE on the now-plain cutaway rim -- this is the full true count, not a 'many hidden on the far side' undercount, because this style's semi-schematic 'unfolded' framing (matching the rest of this set's textbook composition) shows nearly the whole silhouette at once rather than a strict single-viewpoint photograph. DNA re-confirmed at 2x zoom as ONE continuous golden tube looping and coiling back on itself with a single consistent highlight stripe throughout -- no parallel second strand, no double-helix crossing pattern anywhere. Reads clearly as the smallest, simplest, tailless particle in the set: no tail, stub, sheath or baseplate anywhere; nothing hangs below or behind the shell. No baked text, no border (edge scan: uniform charcoal background on all 4 edges, no continuous dark frame line, std <2 on each edge). Chosen as label base (svg_theme).
textbook.burn_note: 2 render calls on this style (1 rejected on a measured count error, not a transient failure); escalation not needed since both ran on gemini-3-pro-image already per the brief's 'start on pro' instruction for this key.

Warm aged paper fills the entire frame edge-to-edge (no separate sheet/mat/frame), soft darker wash halo directly on the paper, fine ink linework, single specimen, small compact faceted shell with painterly golden DNA cutaway and a small dark sepia blob standing in for the internal pilot protein, tiny bronze-tan dots for the DNA-binding protein, no tail/stub/baseplate/sheath anywhere. reference: PASS, with modality explicitly flagged as a STRUCTURAL MODEL, not a photograph. At ~27 nm, ΦX174 is too small for a negative-stain TEM plate to resolve any teachable surface detail, so per SKILL.md's rule that a structural model is the honest option here, the reference chosen is a computational ray-traced rendering of the mature capsid generated from PDB entry 2BPA (McKenna, Ilag & Rossmann 1992 X-ray structure, 3 A resolution), Wikimedia Commons user Fdardel, CC BY-SA 3.0 (GFDL 1.2+ also offered). Downloaded and inspected directly (681x627 px source, square-cropped and upscaled to 1080x1080 by fetch_reference.py -- upscale factor recorded explicitly): shows a single icosahedral capsid as dense green wireframe/ribbon tracing (protein F shell) with distinct cyan wireframe clusters projecting outward at SIX of the twelve vertices -- visible in this particular projection because the other six sit on the model's far side and are self-occluded, which is exactly the 'count what is visible, not what is claimed' pattern the brief calls for, applied to the reference image as much as to the renders. Small magenta patches scattered across the shell interior are consistent with bound interior density (J protein and/or other structured elements) in the crystal structure, though the source page does not caption them explicitly, so this is noted as a plausible reading rather than asserted as confirmed. No baked-in text, scale bar or watermark on the file itself. This is unambiguously a structural-model rendering (ray-traced wireframe, no depth of field, no photographic noise, no substrate) and is labelled as such throughout render.md -- it is not used as an SVG label base (the labelled figures use the science-style renders instead, matching the set's established pattern), it is shown for provenance/comparison only.

4 API render attempts on gemini-3-pro-image, none accepted outright: attempt 1 drew the bacterium's hatch as a confusing separate small character with its own face and measured 0.0 ink on the left raw edge; attempt 2 fixed the single-phage/single-bacterium composition and measured excellent 3-edge raw bleed (top 0.144, left 0.138, right 0.073, bottom 0.050) but filled the hatch AND the bacterium's mouth solid black, violating the 'no solid fills except pupils' rule; attempts 3 and 4 (explicit-negative, then positive-reframing prompt fixes for the black fill) each traded that defect for a WORSE one (attempt 3 kept the black fill AND regressed left bleed to 0.0; attempt 4 fixed the fill but regressed left bleed to 0.0 again and degraded the phage's bump-studding) -- a real instance of the 'describing what NOT to draw reinforces it' prompt-lesson. Per SKILL.md's 'crop, don't re-roll' principle (applied here to a solid-fill defect, not a border), attempt 2 -- the best-composed, best-bled render -- was kept and patched with NO further API call: a morphological opening (17x17 element: erode then reconstruct via dilation, intersected with the original ink mask) isolated the two solid-black regions (hatch disc ~11.6k px, filled mouth ~5.9k px) from the surrounding thin line art purely by local thickness, correctly leaving the two legitimate solid eye pupils untouched (verified: every other opening-surviving component in the image was individually inspected and confirmed to be an allowed pupil, an eyebrow stroke, or the intentionally-bold top body outline, none a shape needing removal). The patched raster was re-traced through coloring.py's own to_bitmap/trace_paths/build_svg. MEASURED EDGE BLEED on the FINAL COMPOSED page (cairosvg render of the actual phix174.coloring.svg at 500px, top 72% = the artwork area, outer 6px ink fraction, threshold 128): top 0.0000 -- unreachable by construction (the speech bubble occupies the top margin on all 119 pages in this atlas, confirmed project-wide, see SKILL.md); bottom 0.076, left 0.144, right 0.048 -- genuine bleed on all three reachable edges, comparable to or better than the sibling pages' accepted numbers, none forming a continuous full-length line. Final image: a small, perfectly round, blunt-bump-studded phage character (correctly legless and tailless -- the deliberate visual contrast with T4's long landing legs and T7's short leg-stubs) floating against a giant smiling bacterium-planet character and handing a tiny scroll toward a plain (now unfilled) porthole hatch; no fight, no bursting, no violence.
